messages:
Marie (AE): Hey team — customer legal asked for a "signed attestation" proving keys are stored/used only in an HSM for their audit. They want: HSM model + firmware, chain-of-trust certs, and a cryptographic proof (nonce challenge) showing key operations happened inside the HSM. Also need pricing for: one-off attestation report + quarterly attestation subscription. Can we do this?

Sanjay (SalesEng): Short answer: yes, but with constraints. We can provide a challenge/response proof (signing a customer nonce) + redacted audit log excerpts and HSM metadata. Full firmware images or raw key material: no. Need legal review for wording. What HSM family did they request (FIPS 140-2 L3 vs L2)?

Marie (AE): They specified FIPS L3 and want evidence of key import path (how CMK was wrapped/imported).

Olivia (Security): We can produce an "attestation letter" that includes HSM make/model, firmware version, KMS architecture diagram, and a signed challenge response. Proposed crypto flow: customer provides a nonce; we execute a sign operation using the customer's KEK inside the HSM and return signature + certificate chain + time-stamped audit-log snippet (redacted PII). That demonstrates custody without revealing key material.

Sanjay (SalesEng): Example PoC flow for SEs: 1) Customer posts nonce (base64). 2) Redwood runs internal job: `hsm.sign(key_id, nonce)` inside HSM. 3) Return `{ signature, signing_cert_chain, audit_log_id }`. Customer verifies signature using cert chain. I can add a tiny code example to the runbook.

kms-bot: security-qa/keyproof-template.pdf uploaded to Google Drive — link: https://drive.redwood.example/s/keyproof-template :rotating_light:

Ben (SalesOps): Pricing notes: one-off attestation (ops labor + legal review + compliance engineer time) ballpark $12k–18k. Ongoing quarterly attestation (report + minimal ops validation) add-on ~$3k/quarter. If they want on-site attestation or physical HSM inspection, add travel + lab fees. Put as NRE line item in SOW.

Marie (AE): Good — also flagged by customer: rotation cannot exceed a 15 min disruption window during cutover, they prefer zero-downtime rollover. Can we commit to that SLA?

Sanjay (SalesEng): We can support near-zero downtime with a shadow-key + dual-read pattern: keep old key active for reads while writes go to new key, then cut reads to new key after verification. This requires SDK/client changes (dual-write/double-check) and routing support in our proxy. Will document limitations (edge cases for long-lived streams). For strict 15m window, we need to run a PoC with their workload to validate.

Olivia (Security): Action items I'm taking: draft attestation wording (include statement: "Redwood performs cryptographic challenge-response attestation; raw key material is never exported from the HSM") and include HSM metadata and redaction rules for logs. Sanjay — include the nonce-signature example and expected audit excerpt in the PoC runbook. Ben — include pricing ranges + SOW language for NRE and quarterly attestation.

Marie (AE): Legal also wants standard clause text that we "do not hold customer raw keys" and that rotation scheduling is customer-led unless a managed rotation add-on is purchased. Can you add that clause?

Ben (SalesOps): Yep. I'll add standard BYOK clause and an optional Managed Rotation addendum offering 24/7 assisted rotation for an additional monthly fee. Draft snippet: "Redwood will perform attestation using cryptographic challenge-response; Redwood will not disclose customer key material. Customer remains responsible for rotation schedule unless Managed Rotation Addendum is in effect."

Sanjay (SalesEng): PoC runbook stub (will expand in GH):
```
# PoC: nonce challenge
nonce = base64url_decode(CUSTOMER_NONCE)
resp = kmsClient.sign(key_id=customer_kek, payload=nonce)
# resp -> { signature: base64, cert_chain_pem, audit_log_id }
# customer: verify signature with cert_chain_pem
```
This verifies ops happened inside HSM without exposing key.

Olivia (Security): Also recommend adding KMIP/PKCS#11 compatibility notes for their audit — include supported APIs and cert thumbprints. I'll attach cert chain and example verification commands in the attestation packet.

Marie (AE): Next steps: Olivia send draft attestation text by EOD tomorrow; Ben insert pricing placeholders into the current SOW draft; Sanjay prepare a 2-hr PoC runbook and verification checklist for the customer to run in their staging env. I'll schedule a call with customer for Thursday. :thumbsup:

Ben (SalesOps): Done — I'll update SOW and ping legal for final clause review. :white_check_mark:

Sanjay (SalesEng): On it. I'll drop the runbook link here once ready.

Olivia (Security): Draft attestation posted: https://drive.redwood.example/s/attestation-draft-v1 — please review.

Marie (AE): Thanks everyone — keeping this thread as the single source of truth.
